issues.legal_issue: The allotment of jointly owned family property to an existing coparcener on partition is not an acquisition by transfer for the purpose of the restriction on eviction for a landlord’s personal need.
material_facts: The premises belonged to an undivided Hindu family, and the tenant had been inducted before the family partition.
On partition, the premises were allotted to a coparcener who already had an antecedent title in the family property.
The landlord applied to evict the tenant for bona fide personal need before five years had elapsed from the partition.
The finding that the landlord satisfied the personal-need ground was upheld and was not challenged before the Supreme Court.
issues.conclusion: The allotment on partition was not an acquisition by transfer within the meaning of section 14(6) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, so that provision did not bar the eviction application.
issues.legal_principle: Section 14(6), read with section 14(1)(e) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958, prevents a landlord who acquires premises by transfer from seeking eviction for personal need before the prescribed period has elapsed. Its object is to prevent a landlord from using a transfer to enable a new owner, previously without title to the premises, to obtain an eviction advantage. Partition transforms the coparceners’ joint title into separate titles to allotted properties; it does not create title in a coparcener who already had an antecedent title. The Court relied on Girja Bai v. Sadashiv Dhundiraj, 43 I.A. 151, and Commissioner of Income-tax, Gujarat v. Keshavlal Lallubhai Patel, 1965 2 S.C.R. 100. Decisions treating partition as a transfer under section 53 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, or section 17(1)(b) of the Indian Registration Act were not decisive because the meaning of transfer depends on the provision’s context and purpose.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_application_for_pe: A landlord sought to evict a tenant from rented premises for the landlord’s personal need in a rent-control proceeding.
predicates.premises_allocated_to_existing_coparcene: A family partition allocated the rented premises to a person who was already a coparcener in the family owning them.
predicates.acquirer_had_antecedent_joint_title: Before the partition, the person receiving the premises had an existing joint title in the family property.
predicates.application_filed_before_waiting_period_: The landlord filed the eviction application before the applicable waiting period had elapsed since the allocation.

issues.definition: When a rent-control personal-need eviction application is filed within the waiting period after premises are allotted on partition to an existing coparcener with antecedent joint title, the allotment is not treated as an acquisition by transfer for the eviction bar.
